newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African insurers' share boom seen nearing end.
newsitem.headline: S.African insurers' share boom seen nearing end.

text.p: South African short-term insurers, once battered by the country's infamous crime wave, have hiked premiums and reaped the profits, but some analysts think the boom period for their share prices may soon be over.
The sector is certainly riding high with four out of the five listed firms showing considerable gains in their market valuation on a year ago.

Last April Mutual and Federal was trading at just below 19 rand, against a price now of 26 rand. Santam has risen from around 25 rand to 35 rand and South African Eagle has jumped from 83 rand to 110 rand.

Guardian National now trades at around 113 rand from 88 rand, while only Commercial Union has lagged the others by dipping from 35 rand a year ago to around 34 rand now, though it hit 41 rand in February this year.
The rise has come on the back of speculation that after being hit hard early on during the crime wave the industry has now found the right premium rates to cope with the problem.

"The escalation of crime found that the premiums they were offering were uneconomical. But now we have seen this massive escalation of the cost of insurance over the last few years," said one local insurance analyst.

Latest figures for 1996 showed a stabilisation in the crime rate, but there are few signs of a drop. At times the situation touches on the surreal as the homes of top politicians from security minister Sydney Mufamadi to deputy president Thabo Mbeki have fallen victim to burglars.
The high premiums now charged by the industry means some investors have been bewitched by the fact that firms are posting margins of up to eight percent on their underwriting.

Usually insurance firms only hope to break even on underwriting and get their real earnings from investing their funds. However, some analysts think the market is ignoring the sector's net asset values.
David Southey, analyst at Edey Rogers, said only SA Eagle's share price was trading at a discount to its net asset value while Mutual & Federal and Santam were trading at premiums.
He doubts there will be any great rise in the sectors valuation. "Their share prices are going to level off for a while," he said.
A correction could be in the offing as more competition puts a cap on premium rises and the belt-tightening South African consumer shops around for the cheapest option.
"The increased competition has been holding back premiums and with real interest rates very high the consumer is hard pressed," Southey said.

Already underwriting profits are showing signs of dropping away. With their last results only Santam and SA Eagle posted rises in underwriting profit while Commercial Union, Guardian National and Mutual & Federal all showed declines.
"Unerwriting profits are starting to slip away," said Egon Trampitsch, analyst at ING Barings.
Other analysts are out and out bears on the sector.
"We think all the short-term insurers -- with the exception of Eagle -- are overvalued," said one who declined to be named, but saw a downward trend in the sector's cycle starting soon.
"As soon as the first one shows a drop in overall profits it will happen," he said.
